To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cooler maritime air advection combined with increasing cloud cover and scattered showers is limiting solar heating and driving trader consensus toward a 27–28°C peak on August 19, with 25–26°C official guidance from Météo-France and the Met Office. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Karachi’s August 20 maximum temperature clusters tightly around 31–33 °C because late-monsoon conditions along the Sindh coast typically produce stable daytime highs in this narrow band.**

Karachi’s location on the Arabian Sea generates a persistent sea breeze that moderates extreme heat, while elevated humidity and frequent cloud cover from the retreating monsoon suppress further warming. Recent model guidance and Pakistan Meteorological Department observations show surface temperatures holding near 31–32 °C amid light westerly flow and minimal rainfall, consistent with the month’s long-term average high of roughly 31–32 °C. Historical data indicate that August maxima rarely deviate sharply from this range without strong synoptic changes, such as a monsoon low or clear-sky heat buildup—neither of which is currently forecast. The market’s heavy weighting on 32 °C (54.5 %) therefore reflects the convergence of climatology, short-range guidance, and the low likelihood of rapid day-to-day shifts before official observations close the market. Updated PMD or international model runs over the next 24 hours remain the key variable that could nudge probabilities among the 31–33 °C outcomes.

eventMetadata.context_description: Singapore’s equatorial location and prevailing southwest monsoon typically produce daytime maxima near 31–32 °C in August, but drier-than-average conditions forecast for the second fortnight of 2026 are elevating temperatures by limiting cloud cover and enhancing solar heating. Official Meteorological Service Singapore guidance issued 17 August projects daily highs of 33–34 °C on most days through the period, with isolated days possibly reaching 35 °C, consistent with recent observations that already exceeded 33 °C on nearly every day in the first half of the month and hit 34.9 °C at Pulau Ubin on 14 August. El Niño-related warmth further supports above-normal readings. These factors concentrate trader probability on 33 °C, with secondary support for 32 °C and limited upside to 34 °C.
